Thanks again for the call earlier today — great to learn more about MedTechCo's constraints and objectives. Per our discussion I've attached a short air‑gap checklist that outlines the standard pieces we validate during an on‑prem/private deployment. Key call notes and open questions below:

3) Whether you can provide a secured jumpbox/bastion for time‑boxed remote support, or if all support needs to be via physical media only.
4) Procurement lead contact + any vendor onboarding constraints (PO process, security questionnaires).

Thanks — happy to walk through the checklist on a quick call.

Diego — thanks for the summary and checklist. Quick answers below, plus I've attached the BOM template with what we have today.

1) Hardware: initial pilot nodes will be built on Dell chassis with 4x NVIDIA A100 80GB per node (we have a mix of A100 and A40 in our estate now; will prioritize A100 for inference).
2) Upgrades: we prefer quarterly planned upgrades. For security patches we can do ad‑hoc but must coordinate a maintenance window (weekday nights).
3) Remote support: Security team is strict — no persistent outbound. We can provision a time‑boxed bastion that can reach Redwood management IPs only for a single session at our discretion, or we can accept signed offline installers via encrypted USB.
4) Procurement: I'll loop in procurement once we have a high‑level SOW.

Notes: HSM (nShield) is available in the rack and we expose PKCS#11 internally. We also have an internal artifact repo (Artifactory) reachable from the cluster.

Attached: medtech_bom_request.xlsx

Hi Samir / Diego — thanks for the context. Short technical answers and recommendations from the SE side: 

1) GPU support: A100 80GB is fully supported by our inference runtime. For pilot we recommend minimum 2 inference pods (redundancy) — a single rack with 2–4 nodes is fine to start depending on concurrency.

2) Offline upgrade flow: we provide a signed, versioned installer bundle. Two supported delivery options:
   - USB bundle (signed with our private key). Customer verifies signature with our public key and installs locally.
   - Internal artifact repo: we can produce a tarball and a signed metadata file; your Artifactory can host the artifact and the installer will validate signatures before installation.

3) Diagnostics & logs: since outbound is restricted, we support an encrypted log bundle export tool that creates a time‑boxed diagnostic bundle (TLS to your internal storage or a file on USB). For time‑boxed remote sessions you can open a bastion with temporary SSH keys; we only request ephemeral access for troubleshooting and supply a limited support runbook.

4) HSM / KMS: PKCS#11 interfaces are supported. We recommend an initial integration test during workshop to confirm key provisioning flow.

5) SLA & support: air‑gapped installs shift some responsibilities to site ops (physical media, power/cooling). We’ll outline a support matrix in the SOW showing which actions require on‑site presence vs remote assistance.

Attachment: airgap_installer_flow_v2.docx — contains diagrams and the signature verification steps.

If this sounds good I can prepare a short tech appendix for the SOW that details install/rollback, rollback keys, and minimum hardware BOM.

—Rishi
